answer_md:
🐾 Here’s how Matt describes his leadership philosophy.

Matt leads with empathy, clarity, and purpose. He describes teams he inherited as “over-processed, under-trusted, waiting for permission instead of owning outcomes.” His focus was to remove those barriers and create an environment where engineers, designers, and product teams could speak honestly, make decisions, and take ownership.

He makes intent explicit, pushes decisions to the people closest to the work, and uses transparency, direct feedback, and open communication. He coaches teams to think clearly, not just execute tasks. His non-negotiables include integrity and respect, psychological safety, and a focus on outcomes, not optics.

At **Accenture’s** Cloud Innovation Center, that included a “permit to fail” learning environment. Teams had avoided risks because they feared blame. Matt organized non-punitive post-mortems, emphasized lessons rather than pointing fingers, and supported lean, low-stakes experiments. Teams applied those lessons to subsequent sprints to prevent recurring failures. In product incubation, he set expectations that early prototypes and user tests would likely fail, then helped teams use that evidence to shape product direction week by week.

He also assembled balanced teams with engineers, product managers, and UX architects, with equal participation and shared accountability. Pair programming, collaborative coding, retrospectives, and knowledge-sharing sessions replaced siloed handoffs.

At the Cloud Innovation Center, teams accelerated delivery **4x** after embracing lean product and modern engineering practices. The balanced-team work also achieved **zero-defect production code** through iterative development and real-time feedback loops.
